newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian 1996 foreign debt rises to 227 mln lats.
newsitem.headline: Latvian 1996 foreign debt rises to 227 mln lats.

text.p: Latvia's 1996 foreign debt rose to 227.36 million lats ($390.5 million) from 1995's 216.65 million lats, the finance ministry said on Friday.
"In 1997, we plan an increase of 100 million lats to 323.8 million lats," Inguna Kupcha, head of the foreign credit management department at the state exchequer, told a news conference.

Debt owed to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) was 32 percent of the total foreign debt while otehr international financial organisations took 26 percent. Some 18 percent was in the form of G24 credits.
Kupcha said three large loan agreements with the World Bank were planned this year for the roads department, upgrading a refuse site and social reform.
The government has issued state guarantees for five loans or for 49.10 million lats.
From January 1, the state exchequer has managed both internal and external debt. The move is aimed to create more efficient debt management.
-- Martinsh Gravitis, Riga Newsroom +371 721 5240 ($ = 0.582 Latvian Lats)
